title: Grandeur Around Gemini South
caption: The Milky Way over Gemini South, Cerro Pachón
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site
credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Gemini South telescope sits high on Cerro Pachón in Chile, with the centre of the Milky Way in the middle of the frame. Below the densest part of the Milky Way lies the constellation Scorpius, and to its right is Sh2-27, a large, deep red emission nebula surrounding the star Zeta Ophiuchi.

The heart of our galaxy is packed with stars and holds a supermassive black hole called Sagittarius A*. Around it stretch the huge dark dust clouds of the Great Rift. They contain many deep-sky objects, including Ptolemy's Cluster (Messier 7) and the Cat's Paw Nebula (NGC 6334), though these are hard to make out in the photograph.
Scorpius is best seen from southern latitudes. Its three-pronged head and its claws reach out from Antares, a bright red supergiant star known as the heart of the scorpion.

understand.summary: A night-sky photograph by Petr Horálek. No camera or exposure details or colour mapping are published.
understand.eye: No exposure details are published, so it is unclear how closely the colours and brightness match what an eye would see from Cerro Pachón.

explore: Petr Horálek, a NOIRLab Audiovisual Ambassador, took the photo during the NOIRLab 2022 Photo Expedition to all of NOIRLab's sites. Fulldome and 360 panorama versions also exist. Gemini South is one half of the International Gemini Observatory, which NSF NOIRLab operates with support in part from the U.S. National Science Foundation.
